correctness.rationale: A length-27 de Bruijn necklace has distinct triples, hence distinct rotations, ordered by their triples. For each two-letter prefix the three predecessors are a permutation of the three letters, since all triples ending in that prefix occur once. Thus the 18 within-block changes are forced; the eight inter-block changes and the wrap comparison give r and c as claimed. Independently enumerated last-column blocks with the predecessor/LF map i -> 9*L[i]+floor(i/3). It is injective already on assigned rows, and an irrevocably closed proper cycle cannot extend to a single cycle. At a leaf all 27 rows return on one cycle, and reversing the predecessor walk spells the cycle with precisely the 27 row triples; that gives one necklace and no extra quotients by reversal or alphabet relabeling. Exact output from `python3 /workspace/review-evidence/02_lf.py` (full log `02_lf.csv` in that directory) matches all 18 cells, total 373248, both marginals and the extrema including the wrap-sensitive minima. Both supplied C++ certificates were inspected as text rather than executed. This establishes only the specified sentinel-free finite case.

value.rationale: This is a natural first ternary case with nine independent local permutation blocks before imposing global connectivity. The joint distribution quantifies both attainment/rareness of the compression-extremal cases and the effect of the wrap comparison, which is lost in a linear-only spectrum. It is a reproducible benchmark for run-enumeration and extremal constructions, not just a recomputation of the de Bruijn total or a new general run law.
